proposed_fields.description_short: Trump said Arizona officials were trying to steal the election after Maricopa County reported ballot-machine problems.
proposed_fields.description_medium: On November 8, 2022, Donald Trump posted that Maricopa County voting machines were not counting ballots and said, “They are trying to steal the election with bad Machines and DELAY.” Reuters reported printer and tabulator problems at some vote centers. A judge rejected a request to extend voting hours, finding no evidence that voters had been prevented from casting ballots. The equipment failures do not establish fraud or a stolen result.
proposed_fields.description_long: During Election Day on November 8, 2022, Maricopa County reported problems with ballot-on-demand printers and tabulators at some vote centers. Donald Trump used the reports to make a specific public accusation. In a post that afternoon he said some machines were not counting votes, then wrote: “People of Arizona: Don’t get out of line until you cast your vote. They are trying to steal the election with bad Machines and DELAY.” Reuters reported the machine problems and the fraud claims made by Trump and other election deniers. In a related court proceeding, a judge rejected a Republican request to extend polling hours because the party had not shown that voters were prevented from casting ballots. Maricopa County’s post-election report documents equipment problems and how ballots were handled; those problems are not evidence that votes were changed or that the election was stolen. The original title’s reference to midterm losses is misleading because Trump’s cited post was made before the results were known. This draft records the statement and the verified dispute without endorsing its allegation.
